title: autocomplete tokens and autofill usability
learningObjectives: Explain autocomplete tokens and autofill usability and build forms with appropriate native HTML behaviour.

understand.concept: The autocomplete attribute provides hints about the purpose of form fields, such as name, email, street-address, postal-code, username, and current-password. Tokens help browsers and assistive technologies understand fields and support autofill.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct autocomplete tokens reduce typing effort and improve usability, especially on mobile. Do not disable helpful autofill without a strong reason, and use the appropriate password tokens for account flows.
understand.analogy: Autocomplete is like a clear label on a storage drawer: the browser can place the right kind of information in the right field.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual form submission and validation follow HTML algorithms and browser behaviour.

explain.narrative: The autocomplete tokens describe the semantic purpose of each field and can help the browser offer stored information.

examples.code: <form><label>Full name <input name='name' autocomplete='name'></label><label>Email <input type='email' name='email' autocomplete='email'></label><label>Postal code <input name='postal' autocomplete='postal-code'></label><label>Username <input name='username' autocomplete='username'></label></form>
examples.explanation: The autocomplete tokens describe the semantic purpose of each field and can help the browser offer stored information.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered form demonstrating the HTML form behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Add autocomplete tokens to a registration form. Include current-password and new-password in an appropriate account form example.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible form using appropriate input types, names, labels, and constraints. Inspect the submitted FormData and explain which controls are successful.
hints: Give every user-facing control a visible label.
Do not trust hidden fields or client-side validation for security.
Test keyboard and mobile input behaviour.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of autocomplete tokens?
options: To describe the expected purpose of form fields to the browser
questions.answer: To describe the expected purpose of form fields to the browser
questions.explanation: Tokens help browsers identify fields and provide appropriate autofill behaviour.

questions.prompt: What is a good form-design principle?
options: Use semantic controls, visible labels, and server-side validation
questions.answer: Use semantic controls, visible labels, and server-side validation
questions.explanation: Accessible forms use appropriate controls and labels, while security validation belongs on the server.
